cases.reason: The format text is the same, but in 2002 data-name-1 may name a data-pointer that is a record of the communication section, qualified by its cd-name. The 2002 qualifier is file-cd-report-qualifier (IN/OF file-name, cd-name or report-name); 2023's is file-report-qualifier only. Records after a CD entry are ordinary 13.14 entries that implicitly redefine the CD area (A.1.1.2), and an output CD's records have no size or category limit (A.1.2.2 SR9), so `01 PTR USAGE POINTER` under `CD CDOUT FOR OUTPUT` is legal 2002 (level 1, as 2002's USAGE rule requires). `FREE PTR OF CDOUT` is therefore in this rule's 2002 scope. The row's witness l1c10_free_multi_operand_arms uses working-storage pointers only and cannot reach it. The probe at --std 2002 compiles it (COBOL0903 obsolete warning only) and prints F0 SET / F1 NULL, which is correct per 14.8.14.3 GR1a. At --std 2023 it is COBOL0902. Side note, not this rule: a level-05 pointer in a CD record draws COBOL1724 (correct, 2002 has the same level-1 rule).

cases.reason: Both formats print the same, but in 2002 identifier-1..4 reach the communication section. A sending or receiving operand may be an implicit CD data-name (SYMBOLIC QUEUE alphanumeric X(12), MESSAGE COUNT 9(6), descriptions that exist only in Annex A). It may also be an item, or a group (for CORRESPONDING), of a record after a CD entry, qualified by the cd-name (2002 file-cd-report-qualifier; 2023 file-report-qualifier). That is the standard way a 2002 program loads a CD before SEND or RECEIVE. The row's evidence (PrintedFormatComplementTests, pb421) uses no CD item. Probe at --std 2002: MOVE to and from SQ and MC, MOVE "XYZ" TO A OF OREC, MOVE 7 TO B IN CDOUT, and MOVE CORRESPONDING W-G TO OREC print M1 QUEUE-A|000042, M2 XYZ|007, M3 XYZ|007 (correct). At --std 2023 it is COBOL0902.
